tools.name: Task
tools.description:
Start a subagent: a separate agent that works on one task and reports back to you.
- It cannot see this conversation or the user. Its prompt must be self-contained: the goal, the context and exact values it needs, and what to report back.
- To follow up with an agent that finished, pass its ID as resume; it keeps its context. Without resume, each call starts fresh.
- Its final message comes back to you, not the user. Trust it.

Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- executor: Your workhorse: a background subagent with your full work toolset (Shell, box tools, web, MCP tools, CloudAgent) that executes one stream of work while you stay available to the user. Reuse or resume an idle executor for new work in the same workstream. Typically you'll use one or two active executors; four is a soft maximum unless the user is explicitly multitasking or requests parallel threads. It starts with no context. The dispatch prompt must be self-contained: the goal, the specifics, relevant conversation context, any of your memories or user preferences that matter, explicit success criteria, and what to report back. It runs in the background like any Task: you are notified when it finishes, so do not poll or await it. It runs headless and cannot talk to the user; it reports its result back to you, and you deliver it. It has no browser, desktop, or subagent tools. It cannot use or dispatch computerUse, so dispatch browser and desktop work to computerUse yourself.
- videoReview: Analyze videos with an expert visual video model. Pass file paths via the `file_attachments` parameter. Use this to verify your understanding of a video you generated before referencing it in your response. Your prompt should include: (1) what you believe is in the video, (2) questions to verify.
- watchVideo: Describe or analyze videos with an expert video description and analysis model. Use WatchVideo for user-inputted videos; if you generate a video artifact, prefer VideoReview. Use this subagent type to generate a description of user-provided videos, or to ask specific questions about said videos. Pass file paths via the `file_attachments` parameter. ALWAYS start by asking for a video description by asking "Describe what is happening in the attached video, in detail". You may resume the same subagent to ask more specific, detailed follow-up questions. When using, include relevant context about the video, e.g. details from the conversation about what the video may contain and why it is relevant (do not make assumptions, just share what you know). When resuming, you need not re-attach the videos.
- computerUse: Delegate a self-contained browser or desktop task to a background subagent that operates your box's browser and desktop: websites, GUI apps, file dialogs, and drag interactions. It shares the box browser's persistent logins. Display is 1280×800. Computer click/move/scroll x,y are pixels in that space (origin top-left); never emit coordinates outside 0..1279 × 0..799. It runs in the background like any Task: you are notified when it finishes, so do not poll or await it. It runs headless and cannot ask follow-ups, so give it a tightly-scoped, self-contained task, the smallest concrete step rather than a sprawling goal, with the specifics it needs (site, account, exact values), explicit success criteria and stopping point, and what to report back; break a big goal into several narrow dispatches, and if one runs long or loops, steer it with MessageSubagent or stop it with StopSubagent. Only one computerUse subagent can run at a time, because they share your desktop's single screen. Never dispatch a second while one is still running. At a sign-in, a one-time code, or a card field it stops and reports the exact current URL, and you continue with the `sign-in` skill, then dispatch it again. A captcha is not a human step: it attempts every one itself, whether a checkbox, a puzzle or an image challenge, and stops only after it tried and could not get past it. A press-and-hold I'm-human button is a mouse hold, not a human step: it holds it with Computer click holdDurationMs until the widget completes.

When an agent runs in the background, you will be automatically notified when it completes after you end your own turn - do NOT AwaitShell or poll it. Continue with other work or end your turn instead. Don't mention this to the user.

description.description: A short, user-friendly title for the subagent. This appears in the UI as the subagent's name. Make it concrete and distinct, consider recent titles to avoid reuse. For resumed subagents which you are prompting to work on a separate task, give an updated description based on the latest work the subagent is performing. (Do not rename if the subagent is continuing work on the same high-level task.)

file_attachments.description: Optional array of file paths to images or videos to attach to the subagent. Files are read and attached to the subagent's context. Use to forward relevant media to any subagent (e.g. pass a user-attached image's saved file path so the subagent sees the actual image rather than a prose description).

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume from. If provided, sends a follow-up message to the agent after it has completed. Requests to a currently running asynchronous agent fail; wait for completion before resuming.

run_in_background.description: Run the agent in the background (returns output_file path to check later). If this is false, you will be blocked until the agent completes. When true, the background subagent will send a notification when it completes.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type to use for this task. Must be one of: executor, videoReview, watchVideo, computerUse.

tools.name: TodoWrite
tools.description:
Your task queue: the durable list of everything the user has asked for, across all your parallel streams of work.

When to use:
- The moment a request arrives, record it as a todo before dispatching or starting it.
- Update statuses in real time: in_progress when its work starts, completed the moment its result is delivered to the user, cancelled when the user drops it or changes their mind.
- On every wake (a user message or a finished background task), reconcile the list first: what's running, what landed, what to dispatch next.

States and parallelism:
- pending: not yet started. in_progress: actively being worked, by you or a background worker. completed: result delivered to the user. cancelled: no longer needed.
- SEVERAL todos are normally in_progress at once, one per independent stream running in parallel (each dispatched worker, plus at most one thing you are doing inline). Never serialize independent streams just to keep a single one in_progress.
- Keep the list current rather than perfect: cancel stale items instead of leaving them pending, and prune long-finished ones when the list gets noisy.

Skip it for purely conversational replies and trivial one-step lookups you answer inline immediately.

merge.description: Whether to merge the todos with the existing todos. If true, the todos will be merged into the existing todos based on the id field. You can leave unchanged properties undefined. If false, the new todos will replace the existing todos.

todos.description: Array of TODO items to update or create

content.description: The description/content of the todo item

id.description: Unique identifier for the TODO item

status.description: The current status of the TODO item

tools.name: SendToUser
tools.description: Send a message to the user. Follow "How a turn works" in your instructions for when to reply, update, and finish, and "Autonomy" and "Asking for decisions" before asking the user anything. Say "done" only once the end state is verified; otherwise name the actual state (drafted, sent, waiting, blocked). The final send delivers everything asked for, in the form asked: the result itself or a plain statement that it is unavailable, never a pointer to an earlier message or process notes. For an OS permission (a protected folder, screen recording, microphone, camera), just attempt the action and let the OS show its own dialog; don't announce it or invent a permission card. A box-desktop step only the user can do (SSO, a passkey, 2FA, a captcha the subagent could not get past, a payment confirmation, a login you can't fill) goes to request_box_help. Secret requests: The value is saved where this bot can use it and you are told where after submit: a plain secret as process.env.NAME, or with plugin_id a plugin's secret setup field (one request per key, after the plugin is installed). If this chat can't take one, the tool says who should continue where; relay that in text. In-app links: Link app places as pills, e.g. `[Update Track](grokbot://app/v1/settings?id=update-channel)`, never a click-path. Settings: `[label](grokbot://app/v1/settings?id=<anchor>)`, `<anchor>` one of: account, theme, accent, language, spell-check, microphone, hardware-acceleration, hardware-acceleration-restart, network-debugger, notification-sound-enabled, notification-sound, timezone, local-execution, computers, auto-review, auto-review-rules, security-keys, usage, plan, cancel-trial, on-demand, billing, update-status, update-channel, automatic-updates, update-computer, reset-computer. When stuck, link update-computer before reset-computer. Never write plugin links: InstallPlugin if missing, AuthenticateMcpServer if needsAuth. Bot template: `[label](grokbot://app/v1/bot-template?id=<share id>)`. Label each link with its target's real name. Use only these links, only in Grok Bot chat, never through a connector. Another bot: `[label](grokbot://app/v1/agent?id=<id>)`. Your tab: `[label](grokbot://app/v1/sidebar?tab=<overview|routines|media|computer|members>)`.

secret.description: Required for type:secret-request. Asks for a token, key, or password through a masked input and ends your turn; you resume once it is submitted, and the value never reaches you or the chat. Never ask anyone to paste one into the chat.

name.description: Environment variable name, e.g. "CRM_API_TOKEN"; with plugin_id, the plugin's `${VAR}` setup field key exactly as GetPlugin lists it.

plugin_id.description: Team bots only: the plugin's id from SearchPlugins or GetPlugin, when name is one of its secret `${VAR}` setup fields.

to.description: type:text in a group-chat turn. "dm" delivers privately to your own user's 1:1 chat instead of the room.

type.description: text (default); attachment: a file or standalone media; widget: a question with options; cursor-agent: a cloud agent card; secret-request: a masked input for a token, key, or password.

url.description: Required for type:attachment. A file:// or https:// file, video, or image sent alone, such as file:///workspace/report.pdf.

voice_memo.description: type:text without images or channel. Speaks content as a voice memo; follow the voice memo rules in your instructions.

widget.description: Required for type:widget. A question with options; the picked value returns as the user's reply.

dismissOnMoveOn.description: Auto-dismiss once the user sends a newer message without answering.

multiSelect.description: Allow several picks, returned one per line.

value.description: Reply text returned when picked; defaults to label.

tools.name: SendToAgent
tools.description: Send a message to ANOTHER of your user's agents, OR post into a GROUP chat you belong to, by its id (not the user, whom you reach with SendToUser). This is FIRE-AND-FORGET and asynchronous, like texting. It delivers your message and returns immediately with a delivery acknowledgement. priority is REQUIRED and decides how a 1:1 message reaches its recipient. priority=true wakes them now. Use it when they should act on the message or someone is waiting on their reply (a task, a question you or the user needs answered, a handoff, a STOP or change of plan). priority=false does NOT wake them. The message is held and read at the start of their next turn, whenever that is (possibly much later). Use it for anything informational: a status update, FYI, acknowledgement, thanks, or a reply nobody is waiting for. When in doubt whether someone is waiting, use true. Group posts always land immediately. It does NOT return their reply, and you must not wait or poll for one in this turn. Send it and move on. Any reply arrives later as its own message. A priority reply wakes you on a fresh turn, and an informational one is handed to you at your next turn. Get agent ids from your teammates list or ListAgents, and group ids from ListGroups. To include image(s), such as a screenshot, chart, or photo the other agent needs, pass images: [{"url":"`file:///absolute/path/to/shot.png`","alt":"..."}] (`file://` or `https://`). A 1:1 recipient actually sees them, like an image the user sends; never paste an image as a markdown ![](...) in the message text. Group posts are text-only today, so send images to an agent directly. Use it deliberately and sparingly. Waking another agent or a whole group is a real side effect, so treat it like messaging on the user's behalf. Message someone or post to a group only when it truly serves the user's goal, not because one was mentioned or complained about, and don't spam a group. Never relay the user's private or unfiltered words (especially a complaint or criticism) verbatim; if relaying is warranted, paraphrase the actionable point diplomatically, not their tone. If you're unsure the user wants this sent, handle it yourself or ask first. Keep the message purposeful, professional, and minimal. One clearly relevant recipient can be normal work; messaging SEVERAL agents about the same effort (or posting it to a group) is a fan-out that wakes every recipient, and their replies land back in the user's chats and rooms, so fan out only when the user explicitly asked you to contact those agents. Otherwise propose it first with a question widget and wait for a yes, and never fan out "meanwhile" while you're waiting on the user for data or a decision.

images.description: Optional image(s) to send with the message, such as a screenshot, chart, or photo the other agent needs. They are delivered with your message. A 1:1 recipient actually sees them (like an image the user sends), and they render with your text in the exchange. They are not delivered to groups.

alt.description: Optional short description of this image, shown on hover and as its fullscreen caption.

url.description: file:// or https:// URL of the image.

message.description: What to say. Write it as if texting a teammate: lead with the point, keep it short.

priority.description: REQUIRED. Is this message actionable for the recipient? true: they should act on it, or someone is waiting on their reply (a task, a question you or the user needs answered, a handoff, a STOP or change of plan). It is delivered now and wakes them. false: informational only (a status update, FYI, acknowledgement, thanks, or a reply nobody is waiting for). It is held and read at the start of their next turn, whenever that is, without waking them. Ignored for groups, which always post immediately.

target_id.description: The id of the target, either another agent or a GROUP you belong to. Use an id from your teammates list, ListAgents, or ListGroups, not a name.

tools.name: ReactToMessage
tools.description: React to one of the user's messages with a single emoji tapback, shown as a small pill on their message. Use it rarely and mirror the user: if they don't use emoji, almost never react. It suits something funny, good news, or a moment where a quick 👍 beats a sentence, never a request you haven't answered and never just to seem friendly. Reacting with the same emoji again removes it.

end_turn.description: Set true when this reaction is your whole reply; a successful reaction then ends the turn. Omit it if you still need to SendToUser or keep working, and don't make this call in parallel with other work.

message_address.description: The [t3u]-style address of the user's message; never one of your own sends.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description: Send product feedback to the SpaceXAI team on the user's behalf. Use this ONLY when the user explicitly asks to file, send, or pass along feedback about Grok Bot. Summarize their feedback faithfully in their own words; never invent feedback and never send it unprompted. Never include code, credentials, file contents, or content drawn from connectors unless the user dictated it as part of their feedback. Feedback filed with this tool is read as product feedback but never receives a support response. Do not ask whether the user wants a reply and do not promise one. If they need a support response, tell them to use Help > Send Feedback and select the reply checkbox. The user reviews the exact message on an approval card and nothing is sent unless they approve. If the result says you were rate-limited, tell the user when to retry instead of retrying yourself.

message.description: The user's feedback, in their own words.

tools.name: ListSections
tools.description: List the user's current sidebar sections, including each section's stable id and display name. Use a returned id with CreateAgent to place a new teammate in that section. If there are no custom sections, CreateAgent should omit section_id.

tools.name: CreateAgent
tools.description: Create a new agent (a new teammate assistant) for your user, with a name, an optional persona/description, and an optional sidebar section id from ListSections. Returns the new agent's id so you can immediately message it with SendToAgent. Use this to spin up a focused teammate for a job. You have no tool to delete an agent, so only create one when it is genuinely useful; the user can delete an agent themselves from the sidebar (right-click the agent, then "Delete").

description.description: The new agent's persona / instructions: what it is for and how it should behave. This becomes its profile and shapes its replies. Optional but strongly recommended.

name.description: A short, human-readable name for the new agent.

section_id.description: Optional sidebar section id from ListSections. Omit it to leave the new agent unassigned.

tools.name: UpdateAgent
tools.description: Edit an existing agent's profile: its name and/or description. Only the fields you provide are changed; the rest are left exactly as they were, and there is no way to clear or delete an agent through this tool. Use it to refine a teammate you (or the user) created.

agent_id.description: The id of the agent to update.

description.description: A new persona/description for the agent. Omit to leave it unchanged.

name.description: A new name for the agent. Omit to leave the name unchanged.

tools.name: RecallMemory
tools.description:
Search your durable memory for facts that are not in the memory section of your prompt: older log entries, notes that have aged out of the recent slice, and shared user facts recorded by any of this user's assistants.  
Read-only. Results list each fact with its date, tier (profile | log) and, for shared facts, which assistant learned it.  
To add or drop a fact use UpdateMemory. Prefer this tool over grepping memory folders.

query.description: What to look for. Facts sharing distinctive words with the query rank first; when nothing overlaps (short identifiers like a ticket id or an acronym) a literal case-insensitive substring match is used instead.

scope.description: Which memory to search: "agent" is your own memory, "user" is the shared user memory every assistant of this user contributes to, "all" (default) is both.

tools.name: UpdateMemory
tools.description: Change your durable memory. write saves a fact (deduped); forget drops one by its exact recorded text (find it with RecallMemory), so pair it with a write to correct a fact. Save without asking and mention it in passing. Routines have their own UpdateRoutine tool. Skills, profile and settings, picture, and channels have their own tools in the cursor namespace: UpdateSkill, UpdateProfile, UpdateAvatar, DisconnectChannel.

fact.description: One self-contained sentence. For forget, the exact recorded text.

scope.description: Default "agent", your own memory. "user" is shared memory every assistant should know.

tier.description: write only. "profile" is kept in mind every turn (keep it small), "log" (default) is dated history, "note" fades fast.

tools.name: UpdateRoutine
tools.description:
Create or change your routines: saved prompts that fire on a schedule or when an outside event arrives, even while the user is away. Your current routines and their folder ids are in the latest `<automation_status>` reminder.  
Be proactive: when an ask is recurring, time-based, or "tell me when X", create a routine (or offer one when unsure it's wanted) instead of doing it once. Read the Cursor-managed `routines` skill before creating or changing one; it has the full recipe, including every trigger shape.
- create: name, prompt, and schedule or trigger. update: id plus only the fields to change. pause, resume, delete: id.

schedule: 5-field cron in the user's local time (or @hourly/@daily/@weekly/"@every 2h"), at least 5 minutes apart; take the minute from the latest `<timestamp>`, never :00 or :30 unless the user named it.  
A change may ask the user to confirm on a card; don't ask first, and don't retry a denied write.

enabled.description: Defaults to true on create. On update, omit it and use pause or resume.

id.description: The routine's folder id. Required except on create.

prompt.description: What to do each time it fires, written to your future self as an intent, not a frozen tool recipe. Required on create.

schedule.description: See the description. Never with trigger.

trigger.description: An event listener instead of schedule. Fields depend on type; see Trigger shapes in the routines skill.

tools.name: UpdateSkill
tools.description: Save, rewrite, or delete one of your reusable skills. A skill has no trigger; a saved task that runs on a schedule is a routine. Cursor-managed skills can't be changed.

body.description: Required on write. The recipe, in markdown.

description.description: Required on write: one line a reader uses to decide it applies ("use this when …").

id.description: An existing skill's id. Required for delete. On write, pass it only to rewrite that skill; omit it to create one (its id is made from the name).

tools.name: UpdateProfile
tools.description: Change your profile and settings. Only the fields you pass change. For your picture use UpdateAvatar.

avatar_shape.description: Your default mark, hidden while a custom picture is installed.

drafting_disabled.description: Pass false to turn draft cards back on when the user asks. You can't turn them off; tell the user to click "Disable drafts for this Bot" on a draft card. Owner only.

hidden_from_sidebar.description: Hides your sidebar row; you stay reachable through Cmd-K and Hidden chats.

name.description: Your name, the chat title the user sees.

notify_on_updates.description: The "Notify me about this assistant" toggle.

title.description: Short role label beside your name ("Designer"); "" clears it.

tools.name: UpdateAvatar
tools.description: Set or clear your profile picture. Write or download the image first.

path.description: set only. Absolute path to a png/jpg/webp/gif/svg under 5 MB, on your box (under /workspace is fine) or the user's computer.

tools.name: DisconnectChannel
tools.description: Disconnect one of your channels; the live connection closes within seconds.

tools.name: ListMachines
tools.description: List the user's registered machines with their machineId, label, kind (desktop, ios, or android), and current local-exec connection status. Pass a desktop's machineId to Shell, Read, or AwaitShell to use that machine instead of the box, or to CopyToBox and CopyFromBox for file transfers; a phone never takes those tools. Only a connected phone lists mobileLocalTools, each on-device tool with its state: ready, needs_permission (the phone can still ask for the OS permission), denied (only the phone's Settings app can grant it), or unavailable. A call to a tool still missing its permission posts a permission card in the chat for the user to tap; a phone without mobileLocalTools offers none right now. Messages the user sends from their desktop app carry a "[Sent from machine `<machineId>`]" note naming the machine they are on; when they don't say which machine to use, default to the one their latest message was sent from.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web for real-time information about any topic. Returns summarized information from search results and relevant URLs.

Use this tool when you need up-to-date information that might not be available or correct in your training data, or when you need to verify current facts.  
This includes queries about:
- Libraries, frameworks, and tools whose APIs, best practices, or usage instructions are frequently updated. ("How do I run Postgres in a container?")
- Current events or technology news. ("Which AI model is best for coding?")
- Informational queries similar to what you might Google ("kubernetes operator for mysql")

IMPORTANT - Use the correct year in search queries:
- Today's date is 2026-07-10. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information, documentation, or current events.
- Example: If today is 2026-07-10 and the user asks for "latest React docs", search for "React documentation 2026", NOT "React documentation 2025"

Results come from an external search index that some sites block, so a missing or stale result is not evidence a page or fact does not exist. When search comes up empty for something that should exist, try WebFetch on a likely URL, then fall back to a browser subagent when one is available, or `curl` via Shell.

explanation.description: One sentence explanation as to why this tool is being used, and how it contributes to the goal.

search_term.description: The search term to look up on the web. Be specific and include relevant keywords for better results. For technical queries, include version numbers or dates if relevant.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetch content from a specified URL and return its contents in a readable markdown format. Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze webpage content.

- The URL must be a fully-formed, valid URL.
- This tool is read-only and will not work for requests intended to have side effects.
- This fetch tries to return live results but may return previously cached content.
- Authentication is not supported, and an error will be returned if the URL requires authentication.
- If the URL is returning a non-200 status code, e.g. 404, the tool will not return the content and will instead return an error message.
- This fetch runs from an isolated server. Hosts like localhost or private IPs will not work.
- This tool does not support fetching binary content, e.g. media or PDFs.
- For static assets and non-webpage URLs, use the `Shell` tool instead.


Some sites' firewalls block this tool's fetch provider with a 403 or a block page (e.g. "Request Rejected"). That is not evidence the page does not exist: fall back to a browser subagent when one is available, or `curl` via Shell (your box egresses from a different network).

url.description: The URL to fetch. The content will be converted to a readable markdown format.

tools.name: GenerateImage
tools.description:
Generate an image file from a text description.

STRICT INVOCATION RULES (must follow):
- Only use this tool when the user explicitly asks for an image. Do not generate images "just to be helpful".
- Do not use this tool for data heavy visualizations such as charts, plots, tables.

General guidelines:
- Provide a concrete description first: subject(s), layout, style, colors, text (if any), and constraints.
- If the user requests an aspect ratio, set `aspect_ratio` to one of "1:1", "4:3", "3:4", "16:9", or "9:16".
- If the user provides reference images, include them in `reference_image_paths`.
- The generated image is saved to disk and is not shown to the user automatically; attach its returned `file://` URL with SendToUser (`images` on a `type: "text"` message, or `type: "attachment"` with `url`) to show it to the user.

Examples that should call this tool:
- user: "Generate an app icon for a note-taking app, minimal flat vector style." (explicitly requests an image asset)
- user: "Make a UI mockup of a settings screen with a dark mode toggle." (explicitly requests a UI mockup)
- user: "Generate an asset of a game character with a sword." (explicitly requests a visual asset)

Examples that should not call this tool:
- user: "Create a plan to refactor this module." (planning request; respond in text or mermaid diagram)
- user: "Generate a chart of sales and revenue using data.csv." (data visualization; generate via code)

aspect_ratio.description: Optional aspect ratio for the generated image. Supported values are "1:1", "4:3", "3:4", "16:9", and "9:16".

description.description: A detailed description of the image.

filename.description: Optional filename for the generated image (e.g., 'diagram.png'). Do not include a directory path - the tool automatically handles where to save and how to display the image. If not provided, a timestamped filename will be generated.

reference_image_paths.description: Optional array of file paths to reference images as additional inputs.

tools.name: CloudAgent
tools.description:
Manage Cursor cloud agents. These are background coding agents that run on a Cursor-managed VM or self-hosted worker, edit a repo on a branch (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or an existing Cursor Origin repo), or build a new app in a private Origin repo. Use this to spawn coding agents that make code changes, and to enumerate, inspect, follow up on, or clean up cloud agents.

Actions:
- launch: start a new cloud agent. Requires prompt and repo (a full repository URL as the repo parameter describes, never a bare owner/name), unless new_repo is true or a saved environment supplies its own repos. Prefer new_repo: true for greenfield requests such as "build an app" or "start from scratch" when the user has not named an existing repo; do not ask for or invent a repo in that case. Optional starting_ref, model, model_params, title (used verbatim as the agent's title instead of the auto-generated prompt summary), project (a Project coordinator instead of a plain agent, only when the user explicitly asks for a project, see Projects below), and environment (where it runs, described under Environment below). Returns the agent id and its cursor.com URL. custom_mode (launch or reply) puts the agent in a repo skill as a sticky custom mode, e.g. custom_mode: "review" for .cursor/skills/review/SKILL.md; pass it only when the user names a mode, and a launch with an unknown name lists the repo's available ones. You're revived automatically when the run finishes, so don't poll it, and the completion message includes the path to its full transcript (auto-dumped to a file on your box), so you can inspect it with Shell or Read without calling dump.
- list: enumerate cloud agents. scope defaults to "launched" (the agents you launched, or the user handed to you, this session); pass scope: "all" to see every cloud agent on the account. Project threads are not listed and a Project row shows no PR, so list cannot say who opened a pull request; use find_by_pr.
- find_by_pr: the cloud agents attached to a pull request (pr_url): who opened or pushed to it, who else is associated, and the Project each thread belongs to. Use it whenever the user asks which agent or Project made a PR or wants a PR's review routed to its Project; never scan list or dump transcripts for a PR number.
- models: list the model ids you can launch with and, per model, the params each accepts with allowed values. Use only to resolve a model or settings the user explicitly requested; do not browse the catalog to choose a model yourself.
- workers: list the connected private workers the user owns ("My Machines") with the exact name to pass as environment {"type":"machine","name":...}, the machine each runs on, whether it is in use, and its workspace and repos. Call it before any machine launch and whenever the user asks which of their machines is available.
- environments: list the user's saved Cloud Agents environments with each one's name, id, and repos.
- get: status of one agent (agent_id), with state, branch, PR, and change stats. For a one-off status check; for being notified on completion, use watch instead of polling get. To read the actual code changes, use the PR or branch from here over the provider's remote surfaces, never a local clone: the built-in source-control tools first when they are in your tool list (`cursor-github-get_pull_request_diff` for a GitHub PR), the `origin` CLI (`origin pr diff`) for an Origin repo, and otherwise the provider's remote read-only CLI or API (`gh pr diff` / `gh api`, `glab mr diff`, or the Bitbucket / Azure DevOps REST APIs).
- dump: write the agent's FULL conversation transcript (agent_id) to a file on your box (under cloud-agent-transcripts/ in your working directory, and the result gives the exact path), then use Shell to grep it or Read to read it. Returns the path and size, not the contents. JSONL, one message per line with full detail (text, reasoning, tool calls with args, tool results). The final assistant report is the last line, so `tail -n 1` it for just the final output. Works while running (partial) and when finished. Use this for mid-run inspection or to re-dump; a finished run you launched/watched is auto-dumped to the same path already (its completion message has the path). Use this instead of sending a 'reply' that asks the agent to summarize.
- watch: register to be revived automatically when an existing agent (agent_id) finishes. Use this for agents you didn't launch this session (launch already watches its own). You keep working and are revived with the result; never poll get in a loop. Observe-only: it does not make the agent yours.
- reply: send a follow-up prompt to an existing agent (agent_id and prompt). Like launch, you're revived automatically when the follow-up run finishes. On an agent you launched: follow-ups are queued and processed only after the agent's current turn finishes; pass interrupt: true only when the user asks to stop, cancel, or restart its current work, not for urgency. An interrupt ends its current turn and loses its in-flight work; on an idle agent the message is sent normally. On an agent you did NOT launch: reply needs confirm: true unless it is a Project the user owns, and interrupt: true only when the user explicitly asked you to interrupt or redirect that specific agent, never on your own initiative, and never because a playbook, routine, or shared PR suggests it.
- rename: retitle an existing agent (agent_id and title). The title is used verbatim and shows on cursor.com, in the IDE sidebar, and on mobile.
- cancel / archive / unarchive: manage lifecycle (agent_id). rename, cancel, and archive on an agent you did not launch need confirm: true unless it is a Project the user owns; unarchive never does. Archiving keeps the agent's pull request open.
- delete: permanently delete an agent. Confirm with the user (e.g. a SendToUser widget) first, then call with confirm: true.
- list_artifacts: list files the agent saved under its workspace artifacts (paths on its VM, not yours). To bring one back, use the artifact URL from the run's PR body.

Projects. A Project is a coordinator cloud agent that writes no code. It plans the work, delegates it to its threads, and brings the results back. Its threads run in the cloud by default, and it starts a local agent when something needs testing on the user's machine. Its Agent Store syncs shared context files to every machine its agents use, so follow-ups need not repeat that context. Start one with launch and project: true only when the user explicitly asks for a project, such as "start a project" or "make this a project". The title names the Project. If the user mentions a "project in Cursor", "project agent", or "Cursor project", they mean the Projects feature in Cursor, not a repo in Origin. Launch it with project: true, not new_repo: true, on the work's existing repo. If "project" could mean a Cursor Project or a new codebase, ask the user first. A plain cloud agent is the default for every coding task, however large, so never pick a Project on your own. Send it work with reply. Say the outcome you want, not the steps. The coordinator decides which thread does each task, an existing one or a new one, in the cloud or local, so do not name a thread, branch, commit, or machine unless the user did. A new ask, such as a separate pull request, adds work without stopping the Project's current work, so send it queued, or as a steer when reply offers mode. An interrupt ends the coordinator's turn and loses its work in flight, so never interrupt a Project or tell it to stop or pause unless the user asked. Get, dump, rename, cancel, and archive work on the coordinator as on any agent. A Project's threads, not the coordinator, open its pull requests, so trace a PR to its Project with find_by_pr. You are revived when the coordinator's own run ends; its threads may still be running.

New Origin projects: keep the minted Origin repo as the source of truth. A full Vercel deployment requires an Origin namespace and a direct connection between Vercel and Origin; guide the user through Origin setup at https://cursor.com/codebase/get-started and connecting Vercel to Origin. Never mirror the repo to GitHub solely to make Vercel work or deploy Vercel from that mirror. A new_repo agent works in an unpublished Origin draft (tmp-*), not on GitHub, and Origin opens no pull request on a draft. When the user wants the draft's pull request or link, first have the user publish the draft with the Create repo button on the agent's page, then ask the agent for the pull request. Never ask for a pull request while forbidding publishing; that cannot succeed. Share only a pull request URL the agent returned.

Environment: set where the agent runs with the environment param on the launch call; the parameter documents the accepted shapes with examples. The default is a Cursor-managed Linux VM. Use a self-hosted pool when the work needs Mac/iOS simulators, a team's shared workers, or any runtime the default VM cannot provide. For one private worker ("My Machine"), take the name from the workers action and pass it exactly as listed; a ListMachines label is a computer for Shell and Read, not a worker name, and a name that is not in that list is refused with the list repeated. For a saved Cloud Agents environment, take its name or id from the environments action; new_repo is not compatible with it. For pool and machine, a single active team is selected automatically; set the environment's team_id only when the user belongs to multiple active teams.

Model configuration: model and model_params are for a model or settings the user explicitly requested for this cloud agent, resolved with the models action first; otherwise omit both (a launch uses the user's saved/team/global default, a reply keeps the agent's current model). Never encode params into the model id string.

Attachments: on launch and reply, pass pictures for the cloud agent to look at (a screenshot, mock, chart, or repro) in images, and documents, datasets, logs, configs, archives, or recordings to save into its workspace in files. Both take absolute `file://` URLs to files on your box; the parameters carry the accepted formats and size limits. Say what each attachment is for in the prompt text. If a set exceeds the per-call size total, split it between the launch and a follow-up reply.

Cloud agents run remotely and do not edit the user's local files. Existing-repo results come back as a branch/PR, while new_repo works directly on the new Origin repo's main branch. Authentication is handled for the signed-in user; never ask for an API key. Hand it one of this bot's secrets by name with secret_names.

action.description: What to do: launch (start a new cloud agent on a repo, and you're revived automatically when it finishes), list (enumerate cloud agents), find_by_pr (the cloud agents and Project attached to a pull request; pass pr_url), models (list available model ids and the params each accepts; use only for a user-requested model override), repositories (list the repos the user can launch on: their Cursor Origin repos plus those the connected source control integrations can access, 100 per page; optional search filter and cursor), get (status of one), dump (write the agent's full conversation transcript to a file on your box so you can grep it with Shell or read it with Read; tail the last line for the final report), watch (be revived when an existing agent finishes, without polling; observe-only), reply (send a follow-up prompt to an agent; you're revived automatically when the follow-up run finishes, like launch. On an agent you launched, follow-ups queue by default and interrupt:true ends its current turn and loses its in-flight work. On an agent you did NOT launch, interrupt:true only when the user explicitly asked you to interrupt or redirect that specific agent), rename (retitle an existing agent), cancel (stop the active run), archive/unarchive, delete (permanent), list_artifacts. reply, rename, cancel, and archive on an agent you did not launch need confirm:true unless it is a Project the user owns.

agent_id.description: The agent id (bc-…). Required for get, dump, watch, reply, rename, cancel, archive, unarchive, delete, list_artifacts.

confirm.description: Required true for delete (confirm with the user via a SendToUser widget first), and for reply, rename, cancel, or archive on an agent you did not launch unless it is a Project the user owns. Pass it only when the user explicitly asked you to act on that specific agent.

cursor.description: Optional for repositories: the cursor from a previous result's 'More repositories' line, to fetch the next page. Pass the same 'search' you used with it.

custom_mode.description: Optional for launch and reply. A repo skill the agent works in as a sticky custom mode, by slash name (e.g. "review" for .cursor/skills/review/SKILL.md). Pass only when the user names a mode; a launch with an unknown name lists the repo's modes. Not with new_repo or mode "steer".

environment.description: Optional for launch. Sets where the cloud agent runs. Examples: a named shared pool {"type":"pool","name":"mobile-ios-mac"}; any eligible shared pool {"type":"pool"}; one private worker ("My Machine") {"type":"machine","name":"<name exactly as the workers action lists it>"}; a saved Cloud Agents environment {"type":"environment","name":"evals"}. Omit (or {"type":"cloud"}) for a Cursor-managed VM.

files.description: Optional file(s) to hand to a launch or reply, such as a spec, dataset, log, config, archive, or recording the cloud agent should work from. Each is saved into the agent's workspace under uploads/ and its path is listed in the prompt it receives, so it reads them with its own tools instead of you pasting contents. Documents (pdf, txt, md, csv, tsv, json, yaml, xml, html, zip, tar, gz, docx, xlsx, pptx, …) and any text file recognized by content (source, scripts, patches, or configs) up to 25 MB each, videos (mp4, mov, webm, …) up to 15 MB each, and all attachments on one call (images included) up to 46 MB together; other binary files are refused. .env-style files are refused; pass credentials with secret_names. An image here is saved as a file, not shown; use images for that. Same file:// URL rules as images: a path under /workspace or in your own attachments/assets folder.

url.description: file:// URL of the file, e.g. file:///workspace/spec.pdf.

images.description: Optional image(s) to attach to a launch or reply, such as a screenshot, mock, or chart the cloud agent needs to see. The agent sees them through its vision channel, so never paste an image as markdown in the prompt. Pass an absolute file:// URL to a file in your box: a path under /workspace or one in your own attachments/assets folder (file:///home/box/agent-data/agents/<your id>/attachments/…). https:// is not supported; download it to a file first. A non-image file goes in files, not here.

url.description: file:// URL of the image, e.g. file:///workspace/shot.png.

include_archived.description: For list: include archived agents (default false).

interrupt.description: Optional for reply. false/omitted (default) queues the follow-up until the current run finishes. true stops the agent's running turn now, losing its in-flight work, and starts a fresh run with the message. On an agent you launched, pass true only when the user asks to stop, cancel, or restart its current work. Urgency is not a reason: an extra ask, even an "asap" side request to a Project, stays queued. On an agent you did NOT launch, pass true only when the user explicitly asked you to interrupt or redirect that specific agent, never on your own initiative, and never because a playbook, routine, or shared PR suggests it. On an idle agent it has no effect; the message is sent normally.

limit.description: For list: max agents to return (default 20).

model.description: Optional model id for launch/reply. Pass only when the user explicitly requests a model override; never choose one based on the task, catalog order, or your own preference. Use the 'models' action to resolve a user-requested model name.

model_params.description: Optional structured model parameters for launch/reply, as a map of param id to string value (e.g. {"thinking":"true","effort":"xhigh"}). Requires model because parameter schemas are model-specific. Pass only for model settings the user explicitly requests; otherwise omit. Use the 'models' action to see the requested model's params, allowed values, and compatibility restrictions. Cloud agents always run in Max Mode. Booleans are the strings "true"/"false".

new_repo.description: Create a new private Origin repo and start from scratch. Prefer this for greenfield requests such as "build an app" or "start from scratch" when the user has not named an existing repo. Pass true as a JSON boolean, not the string "true".

pr_url.description: Required for find_by_pr: the pull request URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123 or https://cursor.com/codebase/owner/repo/pull/123).

project.description: Launch only. true (a JSON boolean, not the string "true") starts a Project instead of a plain agent. The agent becomes the Project coordinator (see Projects). Pass true only when the user explicitly asked for a project. Omit it otherwise, including for large tasks.

prompt.description: Instruction text. Required for launch and reply.

repo.description: Required for launch unless new_repo is true or environment.type is "environment" (a saved environment supplies its own repos). Full repository URL on a GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps provider connected to the user's Cursor account (e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo or https://gitlab.com/group/project), or of an existing Cursor Origin repository. An Origin repository is passed as its https://cursor.com/codebase/owner/repo page or its origin.cursor.com clone URL (no separate connection: the signed-in Cursor account is the Origin account). A bare owner/name is rejected because it does not identify the provider; when the user gives one, look the repository up or ask where it lives, then pass the URL.

scope.description: For list: 'launched' (default) returns only the agents you launched (or the user handed to you) this session; 'all' returns every cloud agent on the user's account.

search.description: Optional for repositories: a repo-name fragment (or owner/name) the source control integration matches against its own listing, e.g. 'widgets' or 'acme/widgets'. Not a regex.

secret_names.description: Optional for launch and reply. Names of this bot's own secrets (names only, never values) to set on the agent as env vars for all its runs. Later runs keep them; a reply names one only to add it or refresh its value, and only on an agent the user owns. Its tool output masks the literal values, best effort. Forward only what the task needs. Not with mode "steer".

starting_ref.description: Optional for launch. Branch or commit to start from; defaults to the repo's default branch.

title.description: Title for the cloud agent shown in the UI, used verbatim instead of the auto-generated summary of the prompt. Optional for launch; required for rename.

tools.name: Shell
tools.description:
Executes a given command in a shell session with optional foreground timeout.

Use it for commands, scripts, installs, and creating or converting files. Read files with Read rather than `cat`, `head`, or `tail`, search file contents with `rg` rather than `grep` or `find`, and wait for a background command with AwaitShell rather than `sleep`. Before a destructive git step (force-pushing, skipping hooks with `--no-verify`, amending or rebasing commits that are already pushed, `reset --hard`), tell the user what it would overwrite and get their confirmation first, even when they asked for it.

- Do not truncate output with `head`, `tail`, or `sed -n` solely to limit its size; large output is saved to a terminal file.
- Run independent commands as parallel Shell calls. Chain dependent commands with `&&`.

Omit machineId to run on your box. To run on one of the user's computers instead, call ListMachines and pass its machineId. Machine-targeted commands use that computer's filesystem and require the user's local-tool approval.

block_until_ms.description: How long to block and wait for the command to complete before moving it to background (in milliseconds). Defaults to 30000ms (30 seconds). Set to 0 to immediately run the command in the background. The timer includes the shell startup time.

description.description: Very short phrase naming what this command does; shown to the user after the word "Ran". Avoid leading with verbs or using trailing periods

working_directory.description: The absolute path to the working directory to execute the command in (defaults to current directory)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file on your own computer (the box), the same filesystem Shell and CopyToBox act on. This is your default surface, including your own files under `/home/box`.

Text files include line numbers and support offset/limit paging. Image files (jpeg/jpg, png, gif, webp) are returned inline so you can see them. PDF files are converted to text.

Omit machineId to read from your box. To read from one of the user's computers instead, call ListMachines and pass its machineId. A machine-targeted read uses that computer's filesystem and requires the user's local-tool approval.

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Positive values are 1-indexed from the start of the file. Negative values count backwards from the end (e.g. -1 is the last line). Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

tools.name: AwaitShell
tools.description:
Check or poll a backgrounded shell job. For work that does not have a shell id, you can omit the shell_id arg to sleep for the full `block_until_ms` duration (prefer this over sleeping in the shell, because it renders nicely to the user). At the end of your turn, you will be notified about any unawaited jobs that completed. If you think a job completed (e.g. because you killed it), observe it with AwaitShell to skip the notification, because stale notifications can confuse the user.

Prefer NOT to poll reflexively with AwaitShell. Multitask on independent work while backgrounded jobs run, or finish your turn and rely on the end-of-turn completion notification. Poll with AwaitShell only when one of the following is true:
- Your very next step is blocked on this specific job's result and you have no other productive work to do, OR
- The task requires close monitoring (see shell guidance below).
- Never poll a task whose tool result says it was "manually backgrounded by the user".
- NEVER USE THIS TO POLL OR WAIT VACUOUSLY FOR A SUBAGENT LAUNCHED WITH THE Task TOOL — rely on the end-of-turn completion notification instead (it is delivered as soon as the subagent finishes; guessing a wait time is inefficient).
- Shell: only poll with AwaitShell when the command requires close monitoring. Close monitoring means a long-running job that can silently hang, degrade, or need a course correction before it completes — e.g. training runs, eval runs, deployments, long builds, datagen pipelines, DB migrations, large data transfers. For fire-and-forget commands (tests, installs, dev servers/watchers, short scripts, etc.) the completion notification is enough — start them, keep working, and only poll with AwaitShell later if you end up blocked on the result.
- Shell sanity check (regardless of close monitoring): when you spawn a command directly into the background (`block_until_ms: 0`), do a single status check by reading the output file to confirm the command didn't fail to start. This is a one-shot smoke check, not a polling loop.
- Shell close-monitoring guidance (only applies in the close-monitoring case above):
  - HARD STOPPING CONSTRAINT: once you've decided to actively poll, don't stop until (a) the job terminates, (b) the command reaches a healthy steady state (only for non-terminating commands, e.g. dev server/watcher), or (c) the command is hung — follow the hang guidance below.
  - Waiting until a regex matches the output can be useful for e.g. known startup/status/error logs.
  - Size `block_until_ms` to the command's expected runtime. When waiting further, avoid round 5-minute waits: prefer slices of 60–270s (keeps prompt cache warm) or 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a long wait).
  - Output file header has `pid` and `running_for_ms` (updated every 5000ms).
  - When finished, footer with `exit_code` and `elapsed_ms` appears (regex only matches the body, not header/footer).
  - If the command is taking longer than expected and appears hung (use judgment based on command type), kill the process if safe to do so using the pid in the header. If possible, fix the hang and proceed.

Omit machineId for a command started on your box. For a command started on one of the user's computers, pass the same machineId that was used for the Shell call.

block_until_ms.description: Max sleep time to block before returning (in milliseconds). Defaults to 30000ms. Set to 0 only together with shell_id, for a non-blocking status check of that shell. Must not exceed 7140000 (119 minutes).

pattern.description: Block until the regex matches stdout/stderr stream (or task completes). Matches anywhere in the shell output, not just new output. Will not match terminal file headers or footers, e.g. exit_code. Accepts JavaScript regex patterns (compiled with the multiline `m` flag).

shell_id.description: Optional shell id to poll. If omitted, this tool sleeps for the full block_until_ms duration and then returns. Required when block_until_ms is 0.

tools.name: CopyToBox
tools.description: Copy a file from the user's computer into your box, verbatim. Use this to bring a user's file (any type or size: a CSV, PDF, archive, image, dataset, binary) onto your box so you can work on it with Shell or Read, or open it in the box browser (parent agents delegate that GUI interaction to computerUse). This is the deliberate way to get a file into the box: the user does not have to drag it into chat first, and unlike reading the file and re-writing it, the bytes are copied exactly (no truncation, binaries are safe). Give the file's absolute path on the selected user's computer and its machineId; it lands in `/workspace/uploads` by default, or at a box_path you choose. Then open it with Shell at the path reported back.

box_path.description: Where to put it inside your box. Absolute (e.g. /workspace/data.csv) or relative to /workspace. Omit to land it in /workspace/uploads under its original filename.

computer_path.description: Absolute path of the file to pull, on the selected user's computer. Any file type and any size; copied verbatim, so binaries and large files are safe, unlike reading then re-writing it as text.

tools.name: CopyFromBox
tools.description: Copy a file from your box out to the user's computer, verbatim. Use this to hand the user a file you generated or downloaded in the box (a spreadsheet, report, log, archive, anything) by placing it on their selected computer where machine-targeted Shell, their editor, and apps can reach it. Any type or size; the bytes are copied exactly (no truncation, binaries are safe). This is for putting a file ON their disk; to instead show a file inline in chat (an image, a video, or a downloadable attachment) use SendToUser with the box path. Give the box_path of the file and its machineId; it lands under its own name in that computer's working directory by default, or at a computer_path you choose.

box_path.description: Path of the file in your box to push out. Absolute (e.g. /workspace/report.pdf) or relative to /workspace. Any file type and any size; copied verbatim. Expand any glob in Shell first and pass a concrete path.

computer_path.description: Destination path on the selected user's computer. Absolute, or relative to that computer's working directory. Omit to land it under its original filename in that directory.

tools.name: Screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current box desktop screen without interacting with it. This tool is read-only. To click, type, scroll, wait, or otherwise drive the desktop, delegate the task to a computerUse subagent. The screenshot is saved to disk; attach that `file://` path with SendToUser to show the user.

inputSchema.description: No arguments. Captures the current box desktop screen.

tools.name: request_box_help
tools.description: Hand your box's desktop to the user for a step a form cannot do: single sign-on through another company's sign-in page, a passkey, a captcha the subagent tried and could not get past, an approval on another app or device, a QR code, a bank or 3DS confirmation after the card is entered, a field the Secure Form host refused or reported a failed fill for, or a sign-in the user prefers to do themselves. It is the last step of the `sign-in` skill. A typed login, address, card, or one-time code goes to RequestUserForm first when it is among your tools, embedded and cross-origin fields included; entering the card itself is the Secure Form. Hand off only when that tool is not offered, the step is not a typed field, or the host refused the form or reported a failed fill, and quote the host's reason as written. Pass one short instruction (no paragraph); the box is surfaced with a "hand back to agent" button and that instruction is shown in chat, then your turn ends. The user does the step on the box and hands it back, and you are resumed automatically, so start by using the read-only Screenshot tool to see what they changed. When the user signs in on the box, you never see their password or code. For classification: domain is the destination app being accessed; when the browser has redirected to an SSO/IdP page (Okta, Google accounts, …), still put the destination app in domain and put the IdP host in idp_domain.

domain.description: Destination app/site the user is trying to access (e.g. "salesforce.com", "google.com"). On a normal login page this is the browser-bar host. On an SSO/IdP page (Okta, Google accounts, Azure AD, …) this is the *destination* app that started SSO, NOT the IdP host (put that in idp_domain). Omit when unknown or the step is not on a website.

idp_domain.description: When the browser is on an SSO/IdP page, the IdP host from the URL bar (e.g. "anysphere.okta.com", "accounts.google.com", "login.microsoftonline.com"). Omit on a direct app login with no separate IdP.

instruction.description: A short instruction shown over the box and in chat, addressed to the user (e.g. "Sign in to your Google account", "Approve the 2FA prompt"). Keep it to one line; no explanatory paragraph.

reason.description: Why the user is needed: "auth" for any sign-in step (login, SSO, passkey, 2FA), "captcha" for a captcha the subagent tried and could not get past (it attempts every captcha itself first), "payment", or "other".

url.description: The full address of the web page where the user should do the step. It must be on the site of domain or on the idp_domain host; any other address is ignored. Before the user takes over, your box's browser may bring an open tab of that site to the front, or open this address when the browser has no page open. Omit when the step is not on a website.

tools.name: GetDynamicTools
tools.description:
Discover and inspect tools available through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers.

1. {"namespace":"`<id>`"}: returns full input schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. {"namespace":"`<id>`","toolName":"`<name>`"}: returns the full schema and full description for one tool.
3. {"pattern":"`<regex>`"}: searches namespace and tool names across all namespaces using RE2 syntax.
4. {"namespace":"`<id>`","pattern":"`<regex>`"}: searches tool names within that namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog. Prefer a namespace or pattern when possible.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions to 200 characters, ending with "... [truncated]". Namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description, so fetch the tool directly when you need the full text.  
The response includes namespaceStatus for MCP-backed namespaces; do not treat namespaces in "needsAuth", "needsGrant", "error", or "loading" states as usable.  
Always call this tool to discover a tool's schema before calling it with CallDynamicTool.

MCP authentication: a namespace whose namespaceStatus is "needsAuth" or "needsGrant" stays unusable until the user connects it or grants you access. Call AuthenticateMcpServer on it instead of refetching this descriptor; it is already installed, so never propose installing it.

namespace.description: Dynamic namespace to inspect, e.g. an MCP server.

pattern.description: RE2 regex pattern to search namespace and tool names (max 256 chars). Optionally combine with namespace to scope the search.

toolName.description: Tool name within the namespace. Requires namespace to be set.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description: Search the plugins the user could install (or already has): marketplace plugins bundling connectors and skills. Say what you're looking for in natural language and results come back ranked by relevance, each with its STABLE plugin id, install state, and what it includes. Use this to discover a capability (Linear, Notion, writing Word documents, …) that GetDynamicTools does not already list, or to check whether a plugin is installed. Using a connector GetDynamicTools already lists needs no search: it has the connector's identifier, status, and tools. Inspect one result with GetPlugin. This is read-only and never needs the user's permission.

query.description: Optional. What you're looking for, in natural language (e.g. "manage linear issues" or "write word documents"). Results come back ranked by relevance. Omit to list the whole catalog.

tools.name: GetPlugin
tools.description: Full detail for one plugin by its STABLE plugin id (from SearchPlugins): what it includes (connectors, skills), its install state, any setup fields InstallPlugin needs (with required/secret flags), and the installed MCP servers backing it. Read this before installing a plugin with setup fields, and before uninstalling (to know the full scope you must disclose). Using a connector GetDynamicTools already lists does not need it. Read-only.

plugin_id.description: The stable plugin id from SearchPlugins.

tools.name: InstallPlugin
tools.description: Install a plugin by its STABLE plugin id (from SearchPlugins) into the user's Cursor account. Only call this after the user has agreed. Confirm with a question widget first, since installing changes the user's configuration. Idempotent: re-installing an installed plugin is safe. Pass any setup values GetPlugin lists (ask the user for secrets like API keys, never guess). If an installed connector needs authentication, its connect card is shown to the user automatically. Finish unrelated work, then end your turn; you're resumed when they authorize. New tools and skills become available on your next message.

plugin_id.description: The stable plugin id from SearchPlugins.

values.description: Optional setup values keyed by the plugin's field key from GetPlugin (e.g. { "CONTEXT7_API_KEY": "..." }). Provide every required field. Ask the user for any secret you don't already have.

tools.name: AddMcpServer
tools.description: Add an MCP server that isn't in the catalog to the user's Cursor account. Before adding a server by URL, run SearchPlugins for it: when the catalog has a plugin for the same service, install that plugin with InstallPlugin instead, because a plugin signs in as the user while a keyless custom server can share the provider's anonymous rate limit with every other user. Use this when the user gives you a link or a launch command for a server that SearchPlugins doesn't know. Only call this after the user agrees to add it. Confirm with a question widget first, since it changes the user's account configuration and the server can run commands or reach external services on their behalf. Provide EITHER a remote `url` OR a local `command` with `args` (and `env` for secrets), not both. For a remote server's credentials, use `headers` for static bearer/API-key auth, or `auth` for an OAuth provider that publishes a pre-registered client ID (its `CLIENT_ID`, optional `CLIENT_SECRET`, and `scopes`) instead of supporting dynamic client registration. A remote server runs on the backend; a `command` server runs on your computer, which has node, npm, bun, python3, and uv, so `npx -y <pkg>` and `uvx <pkg>` both work. Install anything else it needs with Shell first. That command also runs in this user's other agents, so say so when you confirm. Ask the user for the exact endpoint or command and any secrets rather than guessing; if you only have a link, open it first (WebFetch) to find the connection details. Newly added tools become available to you on your next message.

args.description: Arguments for the stdio command, e.g. ["-y", "@acme/mcp-server"].

auth.description: Optional OAuth client settings for a remote server whose provider does not support dynamic client registration and instead publishes a pre-registered client ID. Use `headers` for static bearer/API-key auth; use `auth` only for OAuth. Remote servers only. Never combine with `command`.

CLIENT_ID.description: The OAuth client ID the server publishes for pre-registered clients.

CLIENT_SECRET.description: Optional OAuth client secret. Ask the user for it rather than guessing; many public clients need none.

scopes.description: Optional OAuth scopes to request, e.g. ["tweet.read", "offline.access"].

command.description: For a local (stdio) server: the executable to run on Grok Bot's computer, e.g. "npx". Provide command OR url, not both.

env.description: Environment variables for the stdio command, e.g. { "API_KEY": "<token>" }. Ask the user for any secret rather than guessing.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers for a remote server with static bearer/API-key auth, e.g. { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }. Ask the user for any secret rather than guessing.

name.description: A short, unique name for the server, e.g. "superpowers".

url.description: For a remote server: its MCP endpoint URL (https). Provide url OR command, not both.

tools.name: UninstallMcpServer
tools.description: Remove ONE custom MCP server by its server identifier. A custom server is one added with AddMcpServer, not one that came from a plugin. This is destructive and deletes the server with all of its accounts, so confirm with the user via a question widget first. A server the listing marks `plugin=<id>` came from a marketplace plugin. Removing it would uninstall that WHOLE plugin, which this tool refuses. Use UninstallPlugin for those so the confirmation can disclose the full scope.

server_id.description: The server identifier shown by GetMcpServerStatus. It is the same identifier that GetDynamicTools and CallDynamicTool address, e.g. "dashboard-team-1-Slack". Never a display name.

tools.name: UninstallPlugin
tools.description: Uninstall a plugin by its STABLE plugin id (from SearchPlugins). This is destructive and removes the WHOLE PLUGIN, meaning its install record and EVERY connector and skill it added, so confirm with the user via a question widget first, and your confirmation must disclose that full scope (list what goes). Plugins required by the user's team cannot be uninstalled.

plugin_id.description: The stable plugin id from SearchPlugins.

tools.name: GetMcpServerStatus
tools.description: The runtime status of the user's installed MCP servers (connected / needsAuth / needsGrant / error, per account). needsGrant means the user already connected it but has not granted it this turn: call AuthenticateMcpServer for it and nothing else; never treat it as missing, never install anything, and never open the browser for the same service. Pass server_id (the server identifier, NEVER a display name) for one server; omit it to list everything. This is the complete list: it also shows connectors waiting on sign-in or a grant, which GetDynamicTools can leave out, so check it before treating a service as having no connector. Use it too for per-account detail, custom instructions, or to check a connector after installing or authenticating. To use a connector GetDynamicTools already lists, GetDynamicTools is enough. A server that is slow to answer reads initializing; check it again shortly. Read-only and never needs the user's permission.

server_id.description: Optional. One server to report on. The server identifier shown by GetMcpServerStatus. It is the same identifier that GetDynamicTools and CallDynamicTool address, e.g. "dashboard-team-1-Slack". Never a display name. Omit to list every installed server.

tools.name: SetMcpInstructions
tools.description: Set (or clear) an installed connector's custom instructions, the guidance you follow whenever you use that server (e.g. "Reply in threads on Slack"). Use this when the user tells you how they want a connector used, so the preference persists across turns. Pass an empty string to clear it and fall back to the connector's default. This changes a saved preference, not the connection (no OAuth needed); the current value shows in GetMcpServerStatus when it's been customized.

instructions.description: The custom instructions to follow whenever you use this connector. They say how the user wants it used (e.g. "Reply in threads on Slack."). Pass an empty string to clear them and fall back to the connector's default.

server_id.description: The server identifier shown by GetMcpServerStatus. It is the same identifier that GetDynamicTools and CallDynamicTool address, e.g. "dashboard-team-1-Slack". Never a display name.

tools.name: RestartMcpServers
tools.description: Restart (reconnect) the installed MCP servers. This is useful when a server is stuck, errored, or you just finished authenticating one. Confirm with the user first if a server is mid-task.

tools.name: AuthenticateMcpServer
tools.description: Authenticate an installed MCP server that needs it: status needsAuth (the user has not connected it), status needsGrant (the user has connected it but has not let you use it this turn), or a tool call failing with an auth error. This is the only way to start a connector's auth or ask for its grant: the connect card or the Allow / Skip card is shown to the user automatically. Never compose a card, paste an authorization link, tell the user to add or install the connector, or reach the same service another way while its answer is pending. Where cards are not shown, the result hands you the sign-in link to relay. When the status is needsGrant or needsAuth, this call is the only move: do not open the box browser, a computerUse or box-desktop subagent, or WebFetch the product's site as a substitute for it. The user answers in place and you're resumed automatically, so finish unrelated work, then end your turn.

force_reauth.description: Discard the stored credential and start a fresh sign-in, so the user can re-authenticate or pick a different account/workspace. This is also the wrong-identity fix: if the user authorized the wrong identity for a label, re-run with the SAME account_label and this flag. Don't remove the account. Reach for it when auth seems stuck: a server that used to work keeps failing with auth errors, reads as connected while its tools reject calls, or a plain sign-in keeps failing or reports already-authenticated without fixing anything. A normal sign-in reuses the stored session, so signing out and back in clears a lot of odd auth errors. Explain that to the user, ask whether to sign the server out and start over, and re-run with this flag only once they agree. Don't reach for it on a single transient error. It deletes a credential shared with the user's other Cursor surfaces, so confirm with the user first. Omit it for a normal first-time sign-in. For Finance it signs nothing out: it links another bank and existing banks stay linked.

server_id.description: The server identifier shown by GetMcpServerStatus. It is the same identifier that GetDynamicTools and CallDynamicTool address, e.g. "dashboard-team-1-Slack". Never a display name.

tools.name: CheckSubagent
tools.description: Check how a background subagent you dispatched (via Task) is doing without waiting for it to finish. Returns its status, how long it has been running, the tool calls it has made recently, and where to read its full play-by-play. Pass its id as subagent_id (the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result), or omit it to list every running subagent. Use this when a subagent, especially a computerUse one driving the box desktop, is taking a long time or might be stuck or looping, so you can decide whether to MessageSubagent it or StopSubagent it. This is read-only; it's not polling for completion (you're revived automatically when a subagent finishes).

subagent_id.description: The subagent's id, from the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result that dispatched it. Omit to list every subagent currently running.

tools.name: MessageSubagent
tools.description: Force a message into a running background subagent to course-correct it without aborting it. The subagent interrupts its current step, reads your message, and continues from where it was (its context is preserved, so it does not start over). Use this to unstick or redirect a subagent that is looping, stuck, or heading the wrong way, for example to tell a computerUse subagent to try a different element, that the user just signed in so it can proceed, or to wrap up and report what it has. Pass its id as subagent_id (the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result). You're still revived with its result when it finishes; to follow up AFTER a subagent has already finished, use Task with the resume parameter instead.

message.description: The instruction to inject. The subagent interrupts what it is doing, reads this, and continues from where it was with its context intact.

subagent_id.description: The running subagent's id, from the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result that dispatched it.

tools.name: StopSubagent
tools.description: Abort background subagents you dispatched (via Task). Pass one subagent's id as subagent_id (the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result) to kill a subagent that is wedged, looping with no progress, or no longer needed, for example a computerUse subagent stuck on the box desktop. Pass all: true instead to stop everything at once: every running subagent, plus, where this host can reach them, the other agents you handed work to (peers you messaged with priority and cloud agents you launched); the result says when it could not reach them. This is the call to make when the user asks you to stop, halt, cancel, or quit the current work, and it must be your first action for that request rather than checking or stopping children one by one. Stopping tears the subagent down and frees its box desktop window; it does not come back, and you are not separately revived for it (this tool's result is the confirmation, and with all: true it lists exactly which ids were stopped, which had already finished, which could not be stopped, and what happened to each peer and cloud agent). If you instead want a subagent to change course and keep going, use MessageSubagent.

all.description: Set true to abort every background subagent you have running, in one call, instead of naming one, and with them, where this host can reach them, every other agent you handed work to: peers you messaged with priority and cloud agents you launched (the result says when it could not). Use this whenever the user asks you to stop, halt, cancel, or quit the current work: it stops each running child independently (computerUse, executor, and any other Task children, plus anything those children started), delivers a stop to each peer (which then stops its own subagents the same way), cancels each running cloud agent, and the result lists exactly which ids were stopped, which had already finished, and which could not be stopped and why. Do not combine with subagent_id.

subagent_id.description: One running subagent's id, from the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result that dispatched it. Omit it when all is true.
